strengths: Novel and well-articulated problem identification: The 'sink trap' phenomenon reveals a fundamental disconnect between a model's geometric expressivity and linguistic sensitivity that has not been previously studied
Elegant and well-justified technical solution: Using unconditional priors to stabilize inversion trajectories is simple, effective, and doesn't require auxiliary models or image-based priors
Comprehensive experimental validation: Strong quantitative metrics (diversity ratio, L1, LPIPS, SigLIP), multi-dataset evaluation, multiple baselines, and multiview consistency checks
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-structured paper with effective visualizations, detailed algorithms in appendices, and use of public models (TRELLIS)
Practical impact: Enables high-fidelity text-based 3D shape editing while maintaining global structure and pose consistency, addressing a real limitation of current systems
Insightful theoretical analysis: Section 4's decomposition of language diversity and geometric expressivity provides valuable understanding of text-to-3D model limitations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The core contribution primarily adapts existing null-text inversion techniques from image generation to 3D, with moderate algorithmic innovation
Model-specific approach: Entire framework tightly coupled to TRELLIS; generalization to other 3D generative models is unclear and deferred to future work, limiting broader impact

Narrow evaluation scope: Limited to humanoid/character models (200-280 shapes); no evaluation on diverse object categories (furniture, tools, etc.), raising concerns about generalization beyond characters
Incomplete failure mode resolution: Section 6 acknowledges that extreme OOD cases produce implausible geometries when applying edit prompts, but these failure cases are not addressed or solved
Missing quantitative rigor: Lacks statistical significance testing, error bars/confidence intervals in tables, computational cost analysis, and ablation studies on key hyperparameters
No automatic OOD detection: Requires manual user judgment to apply empty prompts versus text prompts; lacks algorithmic means to automatically detect out-of-distribution conditions
Absent user studies: No human evaluation of editing quality or perceptual naturalness despite claiming practical editing applications

Incomplete theoretical justification: While sink trap is well-characterized empirically, deeper theoretical explanation of why unconditional guidance specifically enables OOD reconstruction is missing
Limited baseline comparisons: VoxHammer fails in 67% of test cases making comparison incomplete; limited comparison with recent 3D-to-3D editing methods and other text-to-3D systems
Hyperparameter complexity: Algorithm 1 involves multiple optimization loops with several hyperparameters; limited sensitivity analysis or ablation studies provided

strengths: Novel problem identification: The 'sink trap' phenomenon—where text prompts fail for out-of-distribution shapes due to misalignment between geometric expressivity and linguistic sensitivity—is a genuine and important limitation that advances understanding of text-to-3D models.

Well-grounded empirical analysis: The diversity analysis (Table 1) systematically demonstrates the phenomenon across multiple models (TRELLIS, LN3DiffL, GaussianAnything), showing this is a general issue rather than artifact.
Sound technical approach: The combination of Euler inversion with null-text optimization is theoretically motivated, clearly described, and algorithmically detailed (Algorithm 1).

Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple evaluation metrics (L1, SigLIP, LPIPS, VLM-based scoring), tests on 3D shapes and 2D images, view-consistent editing results, and reasonable baseline comparisons demonstrate thoroughness.
High-quality practical results: Demonstrates high-fidelity semantic edits on complex non-rigid shapes (Figs. 6, 11-12) with view-consistent rendering, showing meaningful applicability.
Clear presentation and strong visualizations: Effectively communicates the problem (Figs. 1-2) and methodology (Figs. 3-5) with well-written prose.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The core contribution—using unconditional priors via null-text inversion—directly applies established 2D image editing techniques (Null-Text Inversion) to 3D. The methodological innovation is incremental rather than fundamental.

Insufficient theoretical understanding: The sink trap is characterized empirically but lacks theoretical explanation for why this misalignment occurs. No principled criteria for predicting when unconditional inversion is necessary versus when text conditioning suffices.

Narrow evaluation scope: Almost all 3D experiments focus on humanoid/animal characters from DT4D dataset. No evaluation on furniture, buildings, vehicles, or other major shape categories. TRELLIS-generated shapes are synthetic and may not represent realistic OOD scenarios.

Unclear applicability characterization: No clear guidance on when unconditional inversion outperforms text-conditioned approaches. High variance in quantitative metrics (Table 3: ±0.008) makes significance assessment difficult. Fig. 9 shows failures but doesn't systematically characterize failure modes.

Incomplete experimental analysis: Missing ablations on key hyperparameters (CFG scale, optimization steps, learning rate). No computational cost or runtime comparisons. No statistical significance testing despite high measurement variance.
Weak baseline comparisons: VoxHammer fails on ~87% of DT4D samples, making it a poor baseline. Limited comparison to other recent 3D editing methods or non-text-based alternatives.

Insufficient characterization of bounds: Section 6 acknowledges fundamental limitations but provides no quantitative characterization or practical guidance on how far shapes can deviate from training distribution before method fails.

Design choices lack justification: Algorithm 1 shows 10 inner optimization steps and Adam optimizer without ablations or justification. The diversity metric R = Δvis/Δtext is informal and post-hoc without principled motivation.
